title: Hopefully I’m not jinxing it! 🤞 #broadway #musicaltheatre #princessbr...
transcript: Some of y'all don't get how crazy it is that the Princess Bride musical is actually happening. ‘Cause this thing has been on a 20-year long development hell roller coaster without ever seeing the light of day. And now that we're actually getting it, I have some thoughts. So welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback, where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history. This story goes all the way back to 2005 when they started writing a musical version with a score by Adam Guettel, most known for Light in the Piazza, and Floyd Collins. But the story goes that William Goldman was allegedly demanding 75% of the musical's author royalty, and Guettel felt that it was an unfair deal and walked away from the project despite having written the majority of the music already. And as far as I'm aware, the only sliver of this score that's ever been heard by the public was a 10 minute long instrumental medley played at the Hollywood Bowl in 2006. But after the split in 2007, six years went by without a peep. But in 2013, it was announced that Disney would be taking on the project from the ground up. But they started running into problems almost immediately, struggling to find someone willing to write the score. The next major update didn't come until 2019, another six years after that original Disney announcement. David Yazbek, king of the movie-to-musical adaptation, if you will, would be writing the score with Bob Martin and Rick Elice writing the book. But then we went another six years without any news, A weirdly consistent pattern. But in 2025, it was announced that Jeffrey Seller was now producing instead of Disney. Bobby Lopez and Kristen Anderson-Lopez were writing the songs, Yazbek apparently having left the project somewhere along the way without any fanfare or explanation. And for those keeping score at home, this was now the third separate iteration of this musical to be announced without ever playing a single performance. Yazbek had written five or six songs for the show by 2019, possibly more, by the time he left the project. Much like Guettel, none of it ever saw the light of day. So I am sort of excited that the world premiere production has finally been confirmed for 2027 in Chicago, because I do think Princess Bride lends itself to being a good musical. But if I can speak my truth for a moment, I feel like these creative teams have been getting progressively less interesting. I like the Lopezes, I really do. And if they had been the first ones announced, I probably would have been like, “yeah, sure, why not?” But coming after Guettel and Yazbek leaving the project is a tougher pill swallow. Guettel described his score as “driving, swashbuckling, and comedic,” “and uses a completely different set of tools” from his other shows. And Yazbek said that his work had “a weird rock vibe” and “One of the songs goes into jazz waltz at one point.” Whereas, I might guess that this new score is gonna be more safe and broadly palatableby comparison. I admit I'm also a bit disappointed that Bob Martin and Rick Elice are continuing as the book writers. Two artists who, in my subjective opinion, have not written anything good in quite a long time. And I'll leave it up to your imagination to decide just how long I actually mean. Having said that, this might also be the biggest layup they've had in a long time, maybe ever. If they trust the strength of the material, it could very well work. And again, the Lopezes are very talented, so I'm open to being proven wrong. And Alex Timbers might actually be the real ringer here in terms of capturing the humor and heart of the story. So even with my reservations, I remain cautiously optimistic and happy that this project is finally actually happening.
